This study provides a detailed examination of the potential inaccuracies in
the output of contextualized language models when analyzing diachronic semantic
shifts in word meanings. We present an enhanced ensemble method that surpasses
earlier contextualized approaches and apply it to investigate the levels of
semantic change in English vocabulary over the course of 5 decades. Our
results show that contextualized methods may inaccurately predict significant
change in words with little to no actual semantic evolution, or whose
status remains unclear. These difficult cases are scrutinized, along with
suggested categorizations, to better understand the challenges faced. We
conclude that pre-trained contextual language models frequently confuse shifts
in word meanings and contextual fluctuations, leading to inaccurate
assessments of contextualized semantic changes. Additionally, we discuss the
drawbacks of commonly employed evaluation metrics commonly employed in
research on contextualized semantic change. Our code is publicly accessible
at the provided GitHub link.

Active galactic nuclei (AGNs), containing accreting black holes at their center, allow for the investigation of black hole mass and spin through the analysis of electromagnetic spectra. This research uses the Spin-Modified Fundamental Plane of black hole activity, a non-linear model that links radio luminosity, optical or X-ray luminosity, black hole mass, and spin. By applying this model to the quasar sample from the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE), we found a 4-sigma evidence for an anti-correlation between infrared luminosity, a proxy for black hole spin, and Eddington ratio, particularly at high infrared luminosities. This implies a relationship between spin and quasar duty cycle, where super-spin quasar is rare, particularly at high infrared luminosities. This research also finds the spin-modified fundamental plane of quasar is inconsistent with data from the SDSS, suggesting a shift in the modified fundamental plane of one decade. This research also finds a correlation of 2.4 sigma between super-spin quasar and high infrared luminosities.

A distinctive feature of neural development is the rhythmic shifting of cell nuclei
between the upper and lower layers of the neuroepithelial tissue as interkinetic nuclear
migration (IKNM) unfolds. In this study, we utilize extended, high-speed lightsheet and two-photon imaging
techniques in live zebrafish retinas during initial development to gain insights into the underlying mechanisms governing
the behavior of cell nuclei during IKNM. Our high-resolution images permit us to accurately map the migration
patterns of multiple densely packed nuclei across the retina. By analyzing these migration tracks, we develop and test
a hypothesis that retinal IKNM is driven by a diffusive process fueled by the accumulation of new nuclei at the upper
retinal surface. Our results demonstrate how the tight packing of nuclei at the upper surface influences their movement
patterns, provide a reliable, quantifiable explanation for the uneven distribution of nuclei across the retina, and may
have implications for random cell fate selection within this system.

In various image processing tasks, including video compressed sensing and color image demosaicing, images must be separated from coded measurements that represent their superposition. Real-world code patterns, which often have zero-centered distributions and varied standard deviations, yield better reconstruction results compared to simplified alternatives. A novel code pattern is proposed, defined by two primary parameters that characterize its structure. The parameters enable the generation of a wide range of code patterns, which were evaluated alongside traditional methods on compressed sensing and demosaicing tasks. Results show that the proposed model significantly outperforms simplified models in these applications, and its versatility allows customization to improve reconstruction performance. Notably, the proposed model was also effective in chroma-demosaicing, outperforming simplified models and achieving comparable results to state-of-the-art methods.

We've developed a comprehensive hydrodynamic theory that applies to polar active fluids in the presence of randomly distributed inclusions, and our model demonstrates the possibility of overcoming these obstructions to maintain a non-zero overall speed. Contrary to previous assumptions, the dynamics of this specific class of active matter cannot be accurately captured using simplified hydrodynamic models when the spatial environment is two-dimensional up to five-dimensional space; however, we were able to derive precise, dimension-dependent scaling parameters for these dimensions.

Researchers within the same institution often rely on their institutional email as their primary means of communication. Due to their accessibility and private data storage, these emails are vulnerable to cyber threats and can serve as lucrative targets. Our proposed approach aims to examine research institutions' internal communication networks for potential security breaches. Initially, we gathered and analyzed email data from multiple research institutions, including three in Spain and one in Portugal. We applied an SEIR complex network dynamics model to simulate and assess the vulnerability of these networks. Our results indicated that a significant proportion of email accounts, ranging between 54.74% and 86.66%, had been compromised. Furthermore, we observed that the time required for an email infection to reach a critical level (500,000 nodes) varied from 62 to 154 business days, with the Portuguese university exhibiting the shortest infection time. Our method can facilitate a comprehensive security evaluation of academic institutions and provide a basis for enhancing their communication systems.

Inspired by the pseudogap phenomenon in cuprates, we propose a new idea, 
the concept of an "exceptional" van Hove singularity, where a strong 
electron interaction fragments a continuous Fermi surface into disjoint regions. 
We identify this singularity with the merging of two separated Fermi surface 
segments, and demonstrate that it is close to a van Hove singularity, 
reaching it by adjusting a material parameter affecting its dispersion. 
We assert that, in the broader family of cuprate materials, 
the onset of pseudogap is attainable solely through inducing this exceptional 
van Hove singularity, and predict, in response, that there should exist a 
critical temperature, below which the pseudogap is closed regardless of this 
singularity's proximity to a four-fold crossed electron filling.

This paper details a specialized apparatus built for use in Aberdeen Tunnel's laboratory in Hong Kong. The laboratory is uniquely situated to study spallation neutrons produced by cosmic-ray muons with 611 meters of water equivalent in depth. The apparatus consists of six layers of horizontal plastic-scintillator detectors that pinpoint the direction and location of incoming muons. Between these layers, a neutron sensor filled with 650 kilograms of liquid scintillator containing a gadolinium dopant significantly enhances detection efficiency of the produced spallation neutrons. Additionally, the apparatus includes two sets of external detectors, a low-background muon sensor, and auxiliary systems including pressure plates, pumps, and lighting.

Ground-based observations of planetary movements are crucial in validating the findings of space-based missions like Kepler and TESS. Although these missions show that planets are widespread, the success of these missions relies heavily on the use of transit photometry and ground-based radial velocity surveys to determine the physical properties of these celestial bodies. The TESS telescope is capable of identifying planets around bright nearby stars, which are ideal candidates for follow-up observations. We propose the TESS-Keck Survey to investigate various properties of these exoplanets. Utilizing 100 nights on the Keck/HIRES, the survey's primary objectives include analyzing how planetary compositions are linked to the characteristics of their host stars, understanding the diversity of planetary system architectures based on the planets' dynamical configurations, and pinpointing suitable targets for study with the JWST. We introduce a fully automated algorithm for selecting targets, which identified 103 planets across 89 planetary systems in the final TKS dataset. The stars hosting these planets are generally inactive, solar-like, and located within 150 parsecs, and they range in temperature from 4500 to 6500 K, with most of them being brighter than Kepler, making them prime candidates for JWST study. The planets themselves are diverse, including super-Earths, sub-Neptunes, and even an ocean planet, and they are often found in multi-planetary systems that span various distances from their host stars. The target selection

The growth of Information Technology has significantly altered how information is shared, making it necessary to convert printed documents into digital formats.  There has been an increase in fraudulent activities lately.  To prevent such account-related fraud, a system was devised which employs ID card extraction via OCR and NLP for verification purposes.  Optical Character Recognition, a technology that enables the conversion of images to text, can also be used to convert an Indonesian ID card or KTP into text format.  This facilitates easier data entry for service operators.  To enhance accuracy, the extracted text was further corrected using Natural Language Processing.  When tested using 50 Indonesian ID card images, the F-score achieved was 0.78, and the extraction process for each ID card took approximately 4510 milliseconds.

Quantum harmonic oscillators were computationally analyzed in their ground state with either steady-state driving forces or time-varying driving forces, along with an examination of how these factors influence the oscillator's position as they drive it out of equilibrium. Constant driving forces resulted in perfectly harmonic motion when balanced with the oscillator's restoring force, while time-dependent driving forces, such as those modeled by the Raman sideband trap, effectively moved the oscillator's equilibrium point over time and constituted a damped harmonic oscillator due to natural decay. A comparison was made between theoretical calculations and previous simulations of the trap's potential energy, as well as an analysis of the oscillator's equilibrium displacement in relation to the trap's potential.

The Yarkovsky-O'Keefe-Radzievskii-Paddack effect significantly impacts the rotational states of small asteroids by exerting a net torque resulting from solar radiation reflected and re-emitted by the surface. As a consequence of this phenomenon, the rotation period of these asteroids gradually changes, which can be best measured through light curves as the phase shift accumulates over time in a quadratic manner. To study this effect in detail, researchers collected archived data and conducted new photometric observations for asteroids 1992 SK, Geographos, and Toro, before utilizing a light curve inversion method to match their shapes and rotation characteristics. By modeling the YORP effect and incorporating other relevant parameters into their analysis, scientists were able to detect the YORP acceleration in three asteroids and found that the YORP acceleration in all ten detected cases was positive, accelerating their rotations. Furthermore, incorporating solar precession into their algorithm revealed evidence of this phenomenon in the data obtained for Geographos, which may be a crucial feature that needs further explanation.

The youth are increasingly relying on Instagram as a source of information, with political figures leveraging the platform to disseminate opinions and agendas. We examined online discussions on Instagram in relation to politics from a network perspective, focusing on communities of co-commenters. Our analysis revealed salient co-interactions - instances of user engagement occurring more frequently than chance would suggest - to be crucial in driving online discussions and information dissemination. We based our study on 10 weeks of data surrounding key US elections.

We identified increased clusters of online discussion on non-political events surrounding the elections. During these events, users were more likely to start comments on posts sharing opinions, including a higher frequency of political content. We also observed that users were more inclined to co-comment on posts promoting extreme viewpoints. Additionally, we found the inclination to co-comment on political content to be more pronounced during periods elections.

We show that any subgroup of homeomorphisms of a compact surface that fix the boundary, whose action within the surface's interior is highly transitive, cannot be topologically compact when using the compact-open topology's inherited structure.

Precise stellar characteristics are crucial for both astrophysics and exoplanetary science, particularly when studying M-dwarfs. Researchers have developed various empirical relations and theoretical models to determine this accuracy, although the ideal approach remains solving the radiative transfer equations. A careful analysis of the M-dwarf Gliese 367 b's host star was conducted using different methods, yielding a surface gravity value that aligned most closely with empirical estimates with a relative error of less than 10%. This method can also be applied to other stars with exoplanets or Yenchans, making it an accessible, executable, and user-friendly tool that is now part of the MontePython suite for parameter estimation, including the Starfish class in version 0.2.2.

Confining modes at the edge, known as line waves, can propagate on the boundary between two specially designed electromagnetic interfaces that maintain mirror symmetry properties.
Studies have previously analyzed line waves in theory and in practice, revealing their occurrence at both microwave and terahertz frequencies.
It has also been demonstrated that these waves can occur when there's a sudden change from a negative to a positive symmetric resistance and uniform surface reactance present.
Characteristics of line waves include highly confineable mode propagation, polarization dependent on direction, and unique localized field enhancements.
A new study proposes a graphene patch structure, showing that the line waves produced can operate in the optical range.
The design involves a graphene surface integrated with an epsilon near zero substrate, which considers the effects of both dual and uniform reactive impedances.
However, this work specifically focuses on utilizing line waves in dual impedance structures.

Although a key function in database management, the task of listing all answers to a query can become exponentially more complex based on the complexity of the question asked. Research has indicated that adding self-joins to questions increases complexity, particularly when the self-joined elements influence the question's output. To investigate this, we provide a clear measurement of this phenomenon by showing that for certain types of questions, the complexity of their alternatives grows by a factor related to the self-joins, specifically by the number of distinct comparison equations. This factor appears multiple times in the calculation. This result addresses a previously open question and our approach utilizes elements from previous studies on recursive database algorithms, joining tree-like structures efficiently, and order-preserving question mappings. These concepts are directly applied to prove the increased complexity.

Multiple formal models can equivalently define functions that map infinite strings to other infinite strings, including MSO-transducers, streaming transducers, and certain two-way transducers. However, even when restricted to single passes through the input, some functions in these models can still be undecidable by Turing machines with infinite input, despite being defined by two-way transducers with finite domain. In contrast, functions defined by these transducers are not always continuous, despite being undecidable. In an attempt to simplify the descriptive complexity of these functions, we found that using the Wainer Hierarchy alone was insufficient. To address this, we developed a new classification system, the scott-hierarchy, which builds on the Wainer Hierarchy by incorporating higher order sequences. This new hierarchy demonstrates its capability to classify functions defined by first-order transducers. Additionally, we discovered a connection between the levels of the scott-hierarchy and the time required for these functions to process their input.

Researchers have analyzed collision data with an integrated luminosity of 3 inverse femtobarns, and through amplitude analysis of specific two-body decay events, have discovered that the $B^0$ decaying to a pair of $K^*$ mesons exhibits a higher fraction of longitudinal polarization than the $B^0_s$ decaying to the same mesons. Furthermore, this difference in longitudinal polarization was utilized to determine the branching fraction of the $B^0$ decaying to a pair of $K^*$ mesons.

A machine learning technique known as reservoir computing generates a model that mimics complex systems and can be trained on significantly smaller amounts of data compared to alternative methods. The latest version of this approach simplifies training by minimizing the need to adjust numerous parameters. In a recent experiment involving a highly complex system with distinct time scales and multiple coexisting patterns of behavior, a reservoir computer of the new design demonstrated several advantages over its traditional counterpart. Specifically, it used a much smaller amount of data for training, a much shorter time to adjust its performance, a smaller number of parameters to adjust, and a much higher level of accuracy in predicting patterns of behavior, even when those patterns change rapidly. In addition to this performance, it was able to predict areas of stability accurately, further confirming the benefits of this new algorithm.

A new bias-corrected estimator has been created for a mean parameter in a median regression model, which is not normally distributed.  First, we establish the bias correction of the estimator by deriving an explicit, leading-term expression.  Next, we confirm the effectiveness of a related bias-corrected estimator based on a normal distribution approximation.  Then, we conduct a comparative analysis of various estimation methods through numerical simulations.  We also show the advantages of the bias-corrected estimator in real-world data sets.  These include an analysis of heart failure mortality rates over time and another study examining the length of hospital stays for heart failure patients.

To address scalability issues with Eulerian methods for finding optimal controllers and robust value estimates in system-verifiable properties, a second-order numerical differentiation method has been developed for variational Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equations. This algorithm efficiently solves the problem by implicitly computing a sparse polynomial model of the solution, which depends on the system's parameters and time. Building on this framework, two new numerical techniques are presented for calculating the polynomial's coefficients. The first, 'Direct', focuses on smaller systems and aims for high precision, while the 'Indirect' approach, suitable for larger systems, prioritizes finding a stable system over an exact solution. These methods are demonstrated through two case studies, showcasing their ability to accurately solve the Isaacs equation and derive the value of a zero-sum game for systems that were previously infeasible with Eulerian methods.

Multi-Layer Perceptrons are particularly effective at generating accurate
low-dimensional representations of data, such as images, shapes, and light
fields. Despite advancements using periodic activations or positional
encodings, they haven't fully replaced the widespread use of Fourier features
in practice. We introduce an innovative approach that combines and enhances
these methods with a unique dual-MLP framework. This approach uses a directional
representation, provides natural support for video data, achieves remarkable
efficiency, and avoids the limitations of three-dimensional inputs. Our simple
and intuitive setup uses two separate but complementary MLPerceptrons to
represent data, resulting in superior performance at a minimal computational
cost. Notably, our method outperforms the state-of-the-art in NeRF representations,
even with a single image, and excels at evaluating data across multiple views
and video data. Our simple approach uses 200% fewer parameters than the
current leading Fourier-based representation, and at a reduced 100%
parameters, it achieves comparable accuracy. Furthermore, our approach uses
significantly fewer parameters than the existing best practice in video
representations while delivering equal quality. We delve into these findings
further in our paper, providing a comprehensive analysis of our results.

The underlying mechanisms of the ventral temporal cortex's animacy organization remain contentious, suggesting that animacy exists along a spectrum rather than a binary divide. Recent evidence suggests this continuum is influenced by either the Gabor feature or ecological sociality hypothesis. This study analyzed two independently constructed multidimensional feature sets to explain the animacy spectrum in VTC using a regression approach. Our research demonstrates that while both hypotheses contribute to natural scene discrimination, only ecological sociality successfully predicts the VTC animacy continuum. Furthermore, a model combining feature dimensions based on the ecological sociality hypothesis accurately mirrors VTC responses to artificial animal prototypes, suggesting this hypothesis provides the most comprehensive framework for understanding the continuum's organization.

The study proves the nonexistence of Landau-Siegel zeros or confirms quantum unique ergodicity for GL_2 Hecke-Maass newforms at a calculable pace, supported by the broader conclusion that Dirichlet L-function zeros exert a force pushing zeros from all other automorphic L-functions off the s=1 axis.

We have adapted the quantum relational Hoare logic originally proposed in (Unruh, POPL 2019) to incorporate "expectations" into preconditions and postconditions. This modification enables the quantification of pre- and postconditions, thereby allowing for more detailed and nuanced analyses of program performance and verification.

The rapid and significant variation in individual infection rates observed in recent epidemics, notably COVID-19 and SARS, suggests the presence of superspreaders. Despite this, there is currently limited understanding of how superspreader events influence early-stage epidemic expansion or contraction. In order to gain deeper insights, we have established and analyzed a compartmental model, which we have subsequently adapted to stochastic conditions, based on the classic SIR framework. Our model pinpoints the root cause of superspreader events to the uneven distribution of social contacts among individuals. Through our work, we have demonstrated that the presence of superspreaders leads to substantial and unpredictable fluctuations in case numbers, resulting in widely varying daily infection ratios. Notably, our findings suggest that a small fraction of events, either highly expansive or extremely contractive, have a disproportionate impact on our ability to accurately estimate infection rates and predict the course of an epidemic. These extreme events also have a tendency to cluster, further complicating our efforts to assess infection ratios and predict outbreak patterns.

Let's consider a complex topological vector space, denoted as X, along with the collection L(X) of continuous linear operators that act on X. This paper seeks to expand the concept of codiskcyclicity, initially developed for a solitary operator within L(X), to a broader context of operator sets defined as $\Gamma\subset L(X).$ Some key results regarding codiskcyclic collections of operators are proven, accompanied by a codiskcyclicity criterion. Furthermore, we demonstrate its practical utility by investigating the codiskcyclicity of C_0-semigroups comprised of operators.

The paper addresses the problem of bias in vector magnetic field maps, particularly in estimating the component perpendicular to the line-of-sight, Bperp. This issue has been identified previously, but the sources of error were not clearly defined or quantified. The authors argue that the primary cause of bias is using average line integrals to represent local values at the photosphere. The per pixel variance in Bperp, which was understated by prior analyses, was found to vary with magnetic flux concentration and line strength. The variance was found to decrease with increasing concentration and strength. The authors also argue that replacing the integral with the maximum value would reduce variance but introduce a different kind of bias. The authors present an analysis based on Synt_ho maps, which replicate real SIGBOVIA intensity and magnetic field distributions. The results from this simulation were compared with actual Solar data to validate the findings. The authors emphasize that resolving the bias and variance problem is critical for analyzing magnetic reconnection on the Solar surface.

A comprehensive analysis has been conducted to measure the radii of 6097 young star clusters in 31 galaxies from the LEGUS survey. The custom analysis pipeline allowed for a large and contamination-resistant sample, giving us the largest dataset to date of its kind. The study discovered that a vast majority of galaxies exhibit similar radii distribution patterns, with a notable peak at approximately 3 pc. The mass-radius relationship of star clusters in this sample follows a distinct $R_{\mathrm{eff}} \propto M^{0.24}$ pattern. Notably, this relationship applies universally to star clusters under one million solar masses. The age, host galaxy type, and spatial location of star clusters do not significantly affect their size. The study indicates a strong correlation ($k \approx 0.5$) between mass and dispersion, as well as a similar correlation between age and dispersion. The results suggest a robust and unalterable relationship between radii, which may offer a substantial constraint on theoretical models.

We present a novel, direct method for calculating the decay width of hadrons
decaying to two photons, often requiring an indirect estimation via off-shell
form factors. The new method offers an uncomplicated way to study volume effects.
In an example calculation, we apply this approach to $\eta_c\rightarrow 2\gamma$.
Using lattice ensembles with three $N_f=2$ configurations at different lattice
spacings, we derive the final decay width $\Gamma_{\eta_c\gamma\gamma}=6.57(15)_{\textrm{stat}}(8)_{\textrm{syst}}$ keV,
considering systematics in the charm quark mass. This technique can be extended
to additional processes, including radiative meson decays.

A sign problem encountered in Monte Carlo simulations beyond half-filling can be mitigated by transforming the integration path. However, this transformation introduces an additional computational cost associated with the Jacobian determinant in the Boltzmann weight, posing a significant barrier for large-scale simulations. Our proposed architecture, based on a novel application of complex-valued affine coupling layers in neural networks, efficiently circumvents this challenge by achieving linear scaling of the determinant cost. As a result, this method allows us to tackle intractably large systems plagued by a severe sign problem.

By leveraging previously acquired skills and adapting them to unfamiliar tasks without explicit guidance, humans demonstrate impressive cross-task capabilities.
This study aims to enhance the cross-task generalization ability of massive language models in unsupervised settings, with a focus on models like T0 and FLAN.
We introduce a novel, unsupervised retrieval-augmentation method known as ReCross, which employs unlabeled samples to selectively draw from existing data, fine-tune the model for better performance.
The proposed method seamlessly integrates both high-efficiency dense retrieval and a more effective pair-wise re-ranking process to produce outstanding results, surpassing non-retrieval methods and alternative baselines in our experiments.

This research introduces the m-arcsinh Kernel ('m-ar-K') Fast Independent Component Analysis ('FastICA') approach ('m-ar-K-FastICA') for feature extraction, combining kernel-based dimensionality reduction with ICA to overcome the limitations of previous methods. Although the kernel trick offers a powerful way to tackle non-linearity, its effectiveness can be undermined by a lack of open-source and reproducible kernel implementations, especially in complex datasets. The proposed m-ar-K-FastICA approach uses a readily available and adaptable Python library that facilitates collaboration with scikit-learn, providing a more reliable solution for feature extraction even in data sets with high entropy levels and no need for data pre-whitening. Several classification experiments using open-access datasets from diverse domains have shown significant performance improvements, showcasing the enhanced capability of the proposed approach. Furthermore, a comparison with the established FastICA algorithm has validated its superiority in terms of reliability and efficiency.

This work offers an overview of requirements engineering in the gaming sector.
Existing research studies on this topic have been comprehensively examined.
Key characteristics of the gaming industry were identified and their connections to broader market dynamics discussed.
In addition, several potential areas for further research within this field were briefly highlighted.

Optimizing hyperparameters in the private version of the stochastic gradient descent algorithm is a critical issue due to limited access to private datasets for hyperparameter tuning. The development of algorithms that efficiently find optimal hyperparameters for a favorable balance between privacy and performance within a predetermined search space is, therefore, crucial. In this paper, a generalized framework is established to determine an optimal balance between privacy and performance, and three cost-effective algorithms are systematically evaluated: evolutionary optimization, Bayesian methods, and reinforcement learning. The results of an extensive simulation, conducted using the MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets, demonstrate the effectiveness of these algorithms in comparison to a conventional grid search approach. The data obtained from this simulation is also made publicly available.

For a Coxeter system denoted by (W,S), we develop the concept of a boolean complex consisting of involutions within W, mirroring Ragnarsson and Tenner's previous work. By applying discrete Morse theory, we identify the homotopy type of this boolean complex for a significant subset of Coxeter groups, including finite groups, revealing that its homotopy type is equivalent to that of a collection of spheres with dimension |S|-1. Moreover, we derive straightforward, recursive formulas to compute the number of spheres within this collection.

The Euclid satellite, set to launch in 2022, will significantly influence future cosmological research with its Visible and Near Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer instruments. The authors of this study analyzed how correlated readout noise affects in-flight measurements for the NISP detectors and developed an analytical method to quantify this type of noise. Through the NISP Detector Level 1 Processing Pipeline, also designed and tested, the correlated readout noise is minimized by applying a processing sequence to the raw data. The pipeline applies a 2x2 pixel integration, followed by a correction factor calculated on a detector-wide basis to derive the data processing correction factor. The results of simulations and laboratory tests with integrated NISP detectors show that this processing method can reduce the noise correlation, using a technique that does not increase statistical noise, allowing for more accurate data analysis and parameter estimation during scientific analysis.

We applied an advanced statistical approach to examine the composition of 34,410 stars in the Milky Way disk using a vast dataset from the APOGEE-2. The study involved using a two-component model to break down elemental patterns into supernovae types and then comparing observed values to predicted values. The comparison yielded small discrepancies of up to 0.1 dex in some cases. The study revealed relationships between elements including a group sharing similar variations and distinct groups of elements with different behaviors. It also shed light on stars that the model struggled to accurately account for, likely indicating physical variations and small errors in measurements. The study enabled a controlled comparison of different star populations based on factors such as metal content. The findings revealed similar elemental patterns in outer regions of the galaxy, variations in satellite galaxies and star clusters like omega Centauri, and differences in abundance of elements in outer regions compared to inner regions. The study paves the way for a deeper understanding of the formation and chemical evolution of the galaxy.

The COVID-19 pandemic spread globally in early 2020 and caused severe consequences in China, also exacerbating public health anxiety fueled by rampant online rumors. To address this pressing issue, we examined the dynamics of rumor propagation and proposed a method to measure the impact of a rumor by tracking the speed of its new adopters. Utilizing search frequency as a proxy for this metric, we identified the peak and attenuation coefficients of various rumors. Furthermore, we constructed a dynamic model that simulates the diffusion of rumors in an infinite population based on the Borel-Titanini tree and branching process theories, incorporating the peaking coefficient. The model's predictions for mean opinion dynamics proved consistent with empirical empirical data. Notably, we discovered that the rumor extinction probability is determined by the product of the extinction probabilities associated with two distinct branching processes.

A novel approach to measuring the distance to galaxies has been discovered by examining the relationship between absolute and apparent brightness of planetary nebulae, specifically centered on their core absolute and apparent values. This method is highly effective for determining the distances to nearby galaxies. However, the influence of intervening matter, often referred to as intervening hydrogen gas, can distort measurements of apparent brightness. To overcome this challenge, a new technique called reddening correction is used to estimate the extent of this influence and adjust the values of a specific measurement, Fm, to its true, unobstructed form, Fm^0. This study aims to broaden the application of planetary nebulae research to greater distances by conducting a comparative analysis of measured and actual distances to four galaxies - M33, M31, IC 2549, and NGC 2997 - at distances ranging from 3.04 to 26.66 Mpc.

Every day, hospitals around the world gather vast amounts of physiological data from their patients, leading to an escalating interest in conducting statistical analyses to provide better medical diagnoses. These analyses involve complex computations on significant datasets, necessitating high-performance data processing systems that can balance efficiency and simplicity. To address the limitations of existing data processing solutions, we present \emph{LifeStream}, a robust stream processing engine specifically designed to handle physiological data efficiently. LifeStream optimizes performance while providing intuitive temporal query language support, thus striking a balance between ease of programming and computational speed. Furthermore, LifeStream exhibits superior performance, outperforming other leading stream processing engines and hand-tuned numerical libraries by up to $7.5\times$ and $3.2\times$ respectively, on realistic datasets and workload simulations.

This research paper confirms that certain types of curves, specifically those in higher dimensional space, do not fit the classification of Bertrand curves except in two-dimensional Euclidean space. A new category, called the timelike (1,3)-Bertrand curve, is defined to fill this gap and its characteristics are identified for curves in a four-dimensional Euclidean space.

The choice of loss function for a neural network is widely regarded as a key decision with far-reaching implications, given the numerous loss functions developed to date, making it crucial to carefully select one. Despite its significance, research on the topic often omits explicit justification for loss function selection. We contend that this lack of justification reflects an untested assumption prevalent within the deep learning community. In this research, we investigate how loss function impacts performance in a supervised classification context. Our findings reveal that certain, previously underappreciated loss functions, including the KL divergence, can yield superior outcomes compared to established methods, underscoring the need to view loss function choice as a parameter amenable to optimization, rather than a fixed constant.
A stabilizable boundary feedback controller is designed for the Navier-Stokes equations using a linear control scheme with an oblique boundary orientation.

This research aims to advance the understanding of thermomechanical behavior in polymer crystallization. Strain-induced crystallization plays a significant role in polymer mechanical and thermal properties and must be accounted for during production and final product application. To effectively capture its mechanical and thermal impacts, the proposed model utilizes a unique decomposition approach to the deformation gradient and applies the Coleman--Noll procedure and minimum dissipation potential principle to material modeling. The resulting model includes suitable Helmholtz free energy and dissipation potential assumptions, which enables simulation of crystalline region formation, degradation, and temperature changes during cyclic loading tests. Numerical implementation based on the finite element method provides the basis for numerical solutions, which include simulations of material sample microstructure and temperature evolution.

To analyze the impact of external magnetization on doped Bi$_2$Se$_3$ with spin-triplet nematic superconductivity, we computationally investigate magnetic susceptibility in nematic and chiral superconducting states using the Ginzburg-Landau formalism near its critical temperature. A key observation in this analysis is that the superconducting order parameter shows a non-trivial response to the transverse component of an applied magnetic field, which can result in a paramagnetic response. Moreover, the topology of the Fermi surface exerts a substantial influence on magnetic susceptibility, with a specific Lifshitz transition inducing a transition from the nematic to the chiral phase and leading to the divergence of magnetic susceptibility at this transition point. Notably, the interplay between electron-electron interaction and competing phases of superconductivity is also investigated, with results showing that the driving force behind a transition from the nematic to the chiral phase can be the presence of electron-electron interaction, particularly when the energy associated with the exchange interaction is significantly weaker than the kinetic energy loss that arises from switching from a node-less to a node-containing gap structure. A data-driven approach is proposed to provide experimental evidence of this exchange interaction-driven mechanism in Bi$_2$Se$_3$.

One significant issue in Imitation Learning (IL) is that obtaining perfect optimal demonstrations from a teacher is a challenging task due to the complexities involved, especially in robotics. Providing quality feedback is further constrained by the need to supply demonstrations for multiple state actions at once. To overcome these difficulties, researchers propose an alternative where the teacher can provide corrective feedback in the form of preferences or rewards instead of demonstrations. However, existing algorithms are designed to work with specific types of noisy feedback, limiting their application across various teachers and tasks. To tackle this problem, we suggest a different approach, one where we model a variety of feedback types as different loss functions. Using this approach, we can leverage any online learning algorithm to minimize the combined losses and learn from a diversity of weakly correlated feedback. Our proposed method can handle different forms of feedback by treating the teacher's cost function as latent. By applying a general corrective feedback meta-algorithm that unifies prior work, we can achieve similar regret bounds regardless of the type of feedback. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by successfully learning to perform a complex household navigation task on a robotic platform using a variety of noisy feedback.

Continuous phase modulation detection using a non-coherent differential method is renowned for its robustness to phase offset changes, simplicity of implementation, and basic circuit design. Conventional differential detection achieves this by comparing the phase of two successive symbol intervals' signal phases. However, this approach effectively doubles the minimum symbol interval relative to coherent detection, as it requires at least one additional symbol interval for phase differential measurement. We introduce a same-symbol differential detection method, which achieves coherent-level minimum symbol intervals by exploiting phase differences within a single symbol interval. This method is suitable for CPM schemes using multiple symbol intervals for phase evaluation. We provide theoretical performance analysis and simulation results for the same-symbol differential detector, along with an illustrative example using a multiple-symbol-interval M-PSK-CPM scheme to demonstrate its practical application.

New findings from 3D simulations of stellar core collapses have significantly revised our understanding of how much mass collapses into a black hole, with implications for observing gravitational waves when neutron stars collide with each other or with black holes. Our research identifies a simple mathematical formula that accurately represents the 3D simulation results, which can be utilized in models predicting the characteristics of binary systems that emit gravitational waves. When we replace standard models based on 2D simulations and failed supernovae with this new formula in our predictive simulations, we discover a notable increase - up to two orders of magnitude greater in some cases - in predicted detection rates of collisions between black holes and neutron stars. Furthermore, our analysis suggests that a higher proportion of very massive black hole formations, potentially explainable by considering multi-dimensional effects, stellar accretion winds, and photo-disintegration. When we incorporate this explanation into our predictive models, we see an even more significant increase - another order of magnitude greater in some cases - in predicted formation rates of massive black holes, making them more consistent with observed data from the Chandra X-ray telescope.

A previously reported finding from the research of the 1990s and 2000s is that the quantum system's dynamics are highly influenced by the fluctuations of energy, which can be understood through the fourth power of energy fluctuations relative to the mean, a quantity that has a direct equivalent in nuclear collisions known as $\sigma_4$. This relative magnitude is essential for the precise determination of the QCD phase diagram's boundary. However, the current study reveals notable inconsistencies in the reported values of $\sigma_4$ reported in the report of the Collaborative Heavy Ion (CMS) and other experiments, which contradict theoretical predictions based on an underlying statistical framework. This discrepancy underscores the critical nature of this issue, which is now being investigated by the theory community in collaboration with experimentalists to be addressed within the upcoming experiments at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) and the Large Hadron Collider (LHC).

Current deep learning techniques used for removing rain from images have achieved notable success in processing artificially created rainy images.  Nonetheless, their effectiveness drastically drops when confronted with genuine rainy conditions, primarily because they often employ highly simplified models of rain which contrast with the complex real rain scenarios.  This study posits that rain simulation and elimination are mutually interconnected and hence need to be inextricably linked.  To accomplish this, a joint approach to learning real rain simulation and elimination within an integrated disentangled image transformation framework is proposed.  A proposed model involves bidirectional translation of disentangled images in two directions: the translation of real rain images into clear backgrounds and the translation of clear images into real rain images.  This bidirectional process enables the translation of images hidden behind rain into clear images.  Experiments conducted on both synthetic and genuine rain simulations demonstrate that our approach surpasses competing methods.  Furthermore, user studies also confirm that our results are highly satisfactory.  The code related to this study is available on the GitHub repository: https://github.com/Qianhew/DisEntangle.

A prominent paradigm in reward learning utilizes human feedback via comparative evaluations, but their broader adoption is hindered by the expense and labor intensity of these comparisons. To overcome this limitation, we propose grouping multiple comparisons together and allowing human labelers to mark sub-regions of a condensed state space representation, thereby efficiently leveraging human time. Through data visualization techniques, we create an interactive interface for users to label these regions, thereby effectively enhancing the learning agents' performance, even when human labeling time remains constant, across basic Mujoco tasks.

We discuss recent research findings regarding model companions in set theory within the context of ongoing debates in the philosophy of mathematics. Initially, we explore how the concept of model companions is affected by the signature, before specifically examining the dependence of model companions in set theory. Our analysis indicates that the most intrinsic model companions for set theory correspond to $H_{\kappa^+}$ theories, as the infinite cardinal $\kappa$ varies. Furthermore, we highlight that the Continuum problem has a singular solution of $2^{\aleph_0}=\aleph_2$, which aligns with some model companion of enriched set theory containing large cardinal axioms. This model-theoretic framework is justified by a maximality concept reminiscent of Hilbert's axiom of completeness.
This study establishes conditions and proof of existence for a modified Branson-Paneitz equation under Navier boundary conditions on a finite region of n-dimensional Euclidean space.

Evaluating a person's risk of drug abuse is crucial, and online surveys have proven effective for gathering relevant data. The data collection process included a comprehensive range of questions, examining various aspects including personality traits, impulsive behavior, and personal demographics. The study analyzed data from 655 participants, exploring the connections between drug consumption patterns and different variables, as well as comparing the results with a larger dataset. The findings revealed that certain drug users exhibited distinct characteristics in terms of Big Five personality traits and personal demographics, and that our smaller dataset accurately reflected the traits and profiles observed in the larger population. The research also indicates that specific traits and impulsive behavior are linked to different drug consumption patterns, and that predicting the extent of drug use based on these characteristics and demographics is possible with a certain level of accuracy.

Our proposed dataset, ATOMIC, is an exhaustive collection of everyday commonsense reasoning rules comprising nearly a million text-based descriptions.  This atlas of inferential knowledge, structured as conditional relationships between events (If A occurs, one would anticipate B), is organized into categories that mirror the functional purposes of human behavior.  Focusing on reasoning rather than factual truth, ATOMIC provides the intricate logical connections necessary to capture the depth of human understanding of the world.  This underscores the importance of artificial systems that can grasp the nuanced connections among world events, mirroring our own comprehension of the world.  ATOMIC's structured format is particularly amenable to training machines on the complex, interconnected rules that govern our everyday understanding of the world.  As such, it is an essential step toward developing machines that can navigate the real world with the level of adaptability and problem-solving ability we possess.

Portfolio optimization is a critical application in Finance, yet its computational intricacies compel financial institutions to resort to simplified methods. A Hodge Laplacian Portfolio Optimization Method, when combined with the fast multigrid method, can be executed using the recently developed QMLCG solver on a quantum computer. This approach not only addresses the shortcomings of the Monte-Carlo method but also expedites the solution to a discrete portfolio optimization problem. A comprehensive analysis of this new methodology, including a step-by-step breakdown, has been provided to facilitate its implementation via a uniform variational approach. Furthermore, a digital ancilla-free amplitude estimation was incorporated into the algorithm. To validate the efficacy of this new method, a case study was conducted using the STOXX 50 index, illustrating the superior performance of quantum laplacian portfolio optimization in comparison to traditional mean-variance portfolio optimization.

To enhance data efficiency of state-of-the-art end-to-end ASR models and enable them to handle a large amount of unpaired text data in a self-supervised manner, this paper proposes a multilingual and multi-domain ASR system using a simple yet effective multimodal training approach. Two major challenges are identified in the design of such a system: minimizing overfitting in low-resource languages and reducing inference latency due to a multilingual image encoder. To address these issues, a number of innovative techniques are explored, including positionally encoded vision transformers, a gradient-domain knowledge distillation method, and an efficient inference-optimized structure called the Vision-Transformer attention sparsifier. Our team conducted a comprehensive experiment on 9 languages, with data sets ranging from 50k to 3.5 million hours, and our results show that the proposed vision transformer encoder not only significantly reduces training time but also achieves a notable improvement in word error rate, particularly in low-resource languages when a base encoder is distilled.

This analysis addresses the challenge of optimizing cross-sectional area through a specific point within a geometric form. To generalize this concept, the approach is expanded across multiple dimensions. Nonetheless, the optimal average cross-sectional volume cannot be achieved unless cross-sections pass through the centroid of the shape. Therefore, the focus is on stationary shapes with optimal average cross-section properties. A new formula is introduced for average cross-section calculations in any dimension, and the associated equation of stationary shapes is derived. Characteristics of stationary shapes are discussed through mathematical derivation, numerical modeling, and graphical visualization. Additionally, the distinct properties of stationary shapes in 2D, 3D, and 5D are explored and analyzed.

This paper investigates the long-term behavior of a randomly generated uniform parking distribution of size $n$, denoted as $\pi_n$. We establish that the first $k_n$ positions of $\pi_n$, $\pi_n(1)$ through $\pi_n(k_n)$, are asymptotically independent and identically distributed with a uniform probability distribution over the set $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ for any fixed ratio $0 < \liminf \frac{k_n}{\log n} < \infty$. Additionally, we derive an analogous asymptotic independence property for the longest initial consecutive sequence of occupied parking spots. This result allows us to determine the asymptotic behavior of a related statistical measure, $\frac{R_k(n)}{k}$, where $R_k(n)$ represents the longest initial run of consecutive parking spots with consecutive occupied spots of size $k$, for any given $k$.

Measurements of superconducting nanowires, particularly NbN nanowires, indicate the presence of a critical voltage threshold for dc conduction below which coherent quantum phase slips dominate, potentially blocking conduction. The critical voltage of these nanowires is observed to be tunable using an adjacent gate electrode and varies significantly in response to applied voltage, aligning with expected results of quantum interference but exhibiting unanticipated periodic variations. The magnitude of these periodic variations far exceeds predictions based on capacitance alone and presents a discrepancy in understanding this phenomenon, especially after observing sudden period shifts during measurements. The possibility of attributing the behavior to granular Josephson junctions within the nanowires is also considered, offering an alternative explanation for the findings.

The discovery of T-dwarf GJ 229B in 1998 offered initial insight into its composition, yet a detailed analysis based on updated templates has been lacking. By applying a contemporary approach to existing data, including visible and infrared spectra, researchers updated the previously estimated values for its temperature, surface gravity, chemical composition, and color temperature. The analysis confirmed the absence of water vapor and carbon monoxide in the atmosphere, although the findings also highlighted the need for a more comprehensive analysis using a more comprehensive model. The results indicated that the atmosphere is heavily overcooked, potentially due to the object's thermal history, and that the color temperature is more reflective of the surface conditions. The new analysis established the effective temperature at approximately 930 K, although this value is still disputed and may be lower, potentially explaining the absence of water vapor and carbon monoxide. The color temperature could instead be represented by bands of CO, and the color temperature and effective temperature could differ significantly, offering an explanation for these observations. The atmosphere composition was found to contain methane, ammonia, and possibly hydrogen deuteride, and the mass was estimated at 27-42 Earth masses, although the mass estimate remains uncertain and could indicate the presence of a significant amount of heavy elements in the atmosphere.

Our study offers an explanation of how a quark-gluon plasma's temperature and flow velocity affect the Bjorken scaling of structure functions in deep virtual Compton scattering, using thermal operator product expansion. We conducted a detailed analysis of the photon-gluon fusion process at the leading order in the strong interaction constant and derived a general structure function $F_\nu(\xi,T,U_\perp)$ applicable for any value of $\xi$.  Verifying this through a numerical calculation, we identified the specific circumstances under which Bjorken scaling of the $x$-dependent structure function occurs and observed that thermal effects result in a non-zero contribution from the $\xi$-dependent term.  At lower $\xi$ values, Bjorken scaling is more achievable.  We also carried out a numerical analysis of experimental data from the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider to estimate the Bjorken scaling ratio and provide an explanation.

Our proposed approach tackles the challenge of novel view video prediction, taking input from multiple viewpoints. Unlike existing research that relies on narrow angle variations, our network can generate videos from significantly wider angles, up to 45 degrees, without the need for prior knowledge. By processing only RGB frames, we've developed a two-component representation, combining local and global features that enables novel view prediction. Our model achieves remarkable results on real-world datasets NTU-RGB+D and CMU Panoptic, surpassing the state-of-the-art in novel view video prediction, demonstrating significant gains in SSIM, PSNR, and FVD scores of 26.1%, 13.6%, and 60% respectively, without the use of prior views.

In this research, we demonstrate inter-orbital coupling within a two-dimensional photonic lattice by utilizing higher-order modes in silicon disk resonators. We successfully measured this phenomenon and its associated phase shift by applying near-infrared spectroscopy to the photonic lattice. The utilization of higher-order modes in compact silicon devices provides a more feasible approach for emulating complex systems, such as chemical bonds and multi-current atom models, that rely on inter-orbital interactions.

The Ω-baryon, which contains sss quarks and has only been marginally detected in past experiments, has primarily been studied using theoretical methods so far. A study aims to explore this particle's properties utilizing a quark model with linear confining forces. A precomputed dataset of quark masses, sourced from the PDG, is employed for the calculation. A constituent quark approach reveals the mass of the ground state Ω-baryon to be at 1663 MeV, closely matching the average experimental mass of 1672 MeV. Furthermore, this study Aditionally, this study finds the spin states (S) for various resonance states of the Ω-baryon to be 3 for all detected states.

Airborne transmission risk in confined environments like buses is intricately affected by the interplay between turbulent airflow, respiration processes, coughing, and sneezing, as well as various ventilation methods, temperature-driven buoyancy effects, and surface deposition of aerosols. To better understand and model this complex dynamic, we employed an open-source computational tool to analyze and compare the spread of aerosols carried by respiratory particles from the feet of seated passengers in a moving vehicle. Notably, we observed a significant aerosol spread in a bus without any ventilation system, with a notable updraft causing aerosols to settle on the ceiling within 100 seconds, a process accelerated by any ventilation method. The risk of SARS-CoV-2 transmission in buses can be reduced through effective filtration systems, with higher airflow rates resulting in more efficient virus particle exchange with fresh filtered air. Coughing and sneezing pose a greater risk of transmission than gentle exhalation, with the latter leading to a slow spread of aerosols over a larger area. Our analysis also revealed the significant impact of airflow and surface deposition on the spread of aerosols, with the latter playing an important role in slowing down transmission processes.

Building on cutting-edge experimental projects such as HIBEF at the XFEL, our calculations investigate the birefringent scattering of x-rays when interacting with two combined optical lasers, considering various possible outcomes. To aid in detecting quantum vacuum effects experimentally, our analysis focuses particularly on situations where x-ray photons show differences not just in polarization, but also in direction of propagation and potential energy changes.

This note outlines the algorithm devised by J. M. Eisenlohr and S. L. Farris to
systematically generate all fully transitive polyhedra in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. Furthermore, this algorithm is employed to construct a novel polyhedron within three-dimensional Euclidean space.

Broadbent and Lord introduced the concept of unclonable encryption, a unique feature in an encryption scheme where an adversary can't produce two encrypted versions of the same original message from a given ciphertext. Our research expands upon this concept, focusing on several aspects:

  - Flexibility in Usage: We've identified a significant drawback in the previous unclonable encryption constructions by Broadbent and Lord, as they either only guarantee single-use security with public keys or require secure random keys. Our research presents the first construction for both publicly keyed and privately keyed schemes that provide genuine single-user security.

  - Understanding Cloning Definitions: We've identified ambiguity in defining "cloning" in the context of cryptographic security and identified the flaw in the cloning definition used in the previous constructions with random keys.

  - Enhancing Adversarial Resistance: We've identified a gap in the previous unclonable encryption constructions by Broadbent and Lord, as they only address scenarios where the adversary can't observe the original plaintext. Our research presents constructions for public-key and random-key schemes that remain secure even when the adversary can see the original plaintext.

  - Removing Trust Assumptions: We've identified that the previous unclonable encryption constructions by Broadbent and Lord rely on a trusted party to distribute the key, which assumes the adversary can't control this process. This study confirms that physical layer-based authentication is achievable in
Gaussian noise environments, with the caveat that an all-knowing adversary cannot be
beated. An examination of a model comprising encoder, decoder, and adversary was
carried out, with the latter possessing unlimited transmission capabilities and
unlimited access to the transmitted message. It was demonstrated that modifying an
existing communication protocol can enable secure transmission with negligible
efficiency loss, providing an attacker's knowledge does not equate to total access.
Notably, this technique does not rely on the specific characteristics of an attacker's
transmission and does not require a shared secret, thereby facilitating the
implementation of a secure and robust communication system. Furthermore, a secure
transmission capacity model was formulated and found to converge to standard
transmission capacity when no unauthorized access occurs. As a modular solution,
this approach can be applied across multiple system architectures.

We utilized the full tight-binding model and random phase approximation to
explore flat-band plasmons in hole-doped twisted bilayer molybdenum disulfide.
Our calculations showed that lattice relaxation influences plasmon behavior.
When we considered intraband transitions, low-damped, flat plasmons emerged,
while accounting for interband transitions led to plasmon dispersion following
$\sqrt q$ law. The plasmon energies in these materials can be adjusted through
tweaking the twist angles and doping levels. For samples without lattice
relaxations, coexistence of low and high-energy plasmons occurs. Higher doping
levels however eliminate the quasi-flat plasmon. These observations imply that
two conditions must be satisfied: a flat band isolated from the other bands
and adequate doping level to witness the quasi-flat plasmon. The study offers
clues for exploring superconductivity mediated by plasmons in these materials.

This paper expresses the potential function $f$ associated with an almost conformal gradient Ricci soliton on a Sasakian manifold in terms of the scalar field $p$, determining when the potential function is constant, and establishing a link between $f$ and $\lambda$. We also establish a condition for a conformal Ricci soliton to be a gradient Ricci soliton, and provide a characterization of the soliton in terms of its contraction or expansion rate.

Both celestial bodies can experience mass loss due to an expansive outward flow,
often regulated or redirected by magnetic fields that create a surrounding
magnetospheric field. Powerful star winds are generated by the scattering of the
star's radiative force, whereas in smaller stars and our Sun, weaker mass loss is
caused by thermal expansion of the mechanically heated outer layer. This process
can also occur in planets around low-mass stars, resulting in thermal expansion or
mechanical wear on their atmospheres. Magnetospheres in stars arise from wind flow
containment, whereas planetary magnetospheres are shaped by the external impact of
the star's wind. These structures share similar physical features but differ in size,
age, and other characteristics.

The Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect involves a rise in Spin-Orbit Coupling near a strong spin-orbit material's interface with an adjacent layer. This phenomenon has been observed in various systems, including superconductor-heterostructures, magnetic films, and scalar particles, and can lead to interesting effects such as spin-orbit coupling in ferromagnets, time-reversal symmetry breaking in superconductors, and mass gap formation in photons. However, research on electron-photon hybrids受限于 spin-orbit materials' high electrical resistivity and poor conductive properties. In this study, we present ultra-thin van der Waals NbSe$_3$ flakes integrated into optical resonators as a case where Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect leads to significant mass gap formation in electrons with minimal impact on NbSe$_3$'s properties. By analyzing NbSe$_3$'s spin-orbit band structure, we identify the spin-split valence band as the origin of this mass gap, which holds potential applications in valence-band engineering and Spin-Orbit Coupling management.

This paper provides approximate solutions to the fractional time-independent Schrödinger equation in $N$-dimensional space for a generalised Mie-type potential, expressed as $V(r^{\alpha})=A/r^{2\alpha}}+B/r^{\alpha}}+C$, with the fractional parameter $\alpha$ affecting the space variable $r$. The paper presents its results using Adams type integral equations and utilizes q-Matrix representation to express solutions, following the Adams kernel's properties.

We analyze how enforcing a neural network's Lipschitz continuity, as it pertains to input sensitivity, impacts its performance. By examining upper bounds on generalization error, we determine that enforcing this constraint can lead to both beneficial and detrimental effects. To identify the most restrictive neural network representing a target function, we propose an innovative regularization method with a novel proof of convergence. Furthermore, we examine a practical application of this approach in neural network ensembles. Our experiments demonstrate an improvement in test accuracy of up to 8.4% for a ResNet-200 network when employing our method compared to existing regularization techniques. We also find that our network exhibits a 100-fold greater robustness to adversarial attacks while maintaining similar performance, resulting in significantly narrower confidence intervals. To ensure reproducibility, our code is publicly available at https://github.com/cjw255/lipreg.

Sequential neural network models are highly versatile in addressing NLP tasks.
Their sequential design leads to fundamental questions regarding their capacity
to learn complex language hierarchies and grammatical patterns naturally
occurring in human language.
As a case study, we focus on agreement morphology in Basque, a language
with significant structural differences from English and Basque word order
necessitates integrating spatially and temporally distant features for parsing.
By comparing the sequence lengths required for feature integration in Basque
and English, we find that neural networks trained on both languages exhibit
similar limitations in handling feature integration within the same relative
sequence length range.
Our analysis also reveals that sequential models struggle with certain
aspects of Basque morphology, such as the agreement suffixes containing the
plurality feature of the head noun.
To mitigate this, we propose a solution involving explicit subtokenization
of morphemes, which not only resolves this issue but also enhances performance
on the main agreement task by approximately 10%.

HD80606b, a planet that passes directly in front of its host star, undergoes a significant 1000-fold increase in the heat it receives due to its highly eccentric 111-day orbit. As the planet rapidly moves close to its star, its surface temperature jumps dramatically from 446K to over 1300K, causing the released energy to exceed that of its host star by a factor of 10^-7 at its peak. Our study aims to examine the effect this energy surge has on the system's overall dynamics. A detailed analysis was conducted to assess the impact of this additional energy on several factors, including: a) how much of the released energy escapes into space, the amount of surface material that is reabsorbed, and any permanent changes to the planet's interior structure; b) the effect on the system's gravitational balance; and c) the impact on any moons orbiting the planet. Most factors initially appeared to have negligible effects, yet the high energy output of the planet caused a substantial outflow of gas, with mass loss rates during the most recent several hours amounting to 10^-5 to 10^-6 of the planet's total mass each second. As a result, the energy released by the planet actually slows this expansion, making it more compact than expected, causing a 10% increase in its central pressure, and potentially affecting any internal weather patterns. Customized digital games successfully encourage motivation in repetitive exercises required for motor rehabilitation; nevertheless, developing adjustments that cater to both therapy and enjoyment objectives poses a challenge. To tackle this issue, we propose an approach where an initial statistical model of game performance identifies specific settings that mirror players' typical behavior, even in the face of diminished control. This approach is exemplified through a practical application involving upper limb rehabilitation and a specially designed controller for the Pac-Man game. Collaborative sessions between occupational therapists and game developers resulted in the identification of two key factors that affect the gameplay experience and influence rehabilitation adjustments. Experimental measurements of the participants' interaction with the modified game revealed that our low-latency statistical model accurately identifies optimal parameter values that reproduce baseline gameplay under controlled conditions. This methodology holds potential for addressing balance problems related to the design of gamified systems, particularly those involving conflicting requirements for physical involvement and subjectively enjoyable experiences.

Our research offers a variational approximation, drawing from the Ambrosio-Tortorelli model, to quantify brittle fracture energies in complex, piecewise-rigid structures, applicable to both nonlinear and linearised elasticity frameworks.

We investigate the possibility of lepton-flavour non-universality in certain processes at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). To this end, we focus on Drell-Yan ditau production and calculate precise corrections to this process, taking into account the effects of quantum chromodynamics at the next-to-leading order. A specialized code is developed to efficiently generate these corrections, allowing for more accurate simulations of ditau events. By applying these simulations to recent LHC data, we can place constraints on a type of exotic particle, known as vector leptoquarks, based on their mass and coupling strength. This code is an important tool for ongoing and future searches for vector leptoquarks at the LHC, particularly those involving the collision of protons at high energies.

Radiation exposure during positron emission tomography (PET) scans restricts their usage for sensitive groups, such as pregnant women and young individuals requiring frequent imaging, due to compromised image quality from lower doses or shorter scan times. Deep-learning models have made significant advancements in enhancing PET images by translating low-quality PET scans onto high-quality MRI images, thus potentially allowing the same enhancement gains that have been achieved with traditional methods. Nonetheless, bias present in the training data of these models can present their application with similar limitations. To overcome this challenge, we introduce petGan, a generative adversarial network framework developed using a simulation-based approach, enabling it to enhance low-dose and short-acquisition PET images while accounting for the stochastic nature of PET imaging processes, the quantum nature of the sine-gram transformation, and prior to adversarial training, we pre-condition the input images to reduce bias by transforming them into intermediate images that better conform to the distribution of high-quality PET images. The model of petGan was trained on simulation data representing 18F-PET scans with various levels of noise and spatial resolution enhancements, it demonstrated significant improvement in quantitative metrics when compared to various deep learning baselines, and it displayed robust performance when tested on real low-dose and short-acquisition PET scans.

The issue of tailoring news to individuals' interests while respecting their data remains unresolved. Growing worries about over-collected data and its unintended use have motivated our research on balancing personalization and privacy. Our experience creating personalized content platforms that protect users' confidentiality has sparked an investigation into users' attitudes towards these topics. A conducted survey revealed the opinions of various age groups regarding personalization and privacy. In this research, we are sharing our key discoveries with publishers and the community to inform the design and development of next-generation news recommender systems, which should prioritize the human user and achieve a harmonious balance between personalization and privacy.

A linguistic analysis known as centering theory (CT) explains how coherence in conversations emerges from the connections between successive statements. This paper explores the link between CT and advanced computer systems that identify relationships within a text. By developing specific metrics and a search-based method, the study examines if modern computer systems that recognize connections within a text align with the principles of CT. The analysis indicates a correlation between the systems' ability to recognize connections and their ability to model the coherence of the text, but also reveals that these computer systems are not necessarily improved by considering the ideas underlying CT. Furthermore, the study finds that these computer systems already incorporate the coherence information required to recognize connections within the text, making CT's contribution limited. Additionally, the study discusses aspects that CT fails to account for, including variations in statement importance and their impact on connections within the text.

We have devised three new parameterized algorithms for identifying whether a directed graph can be represented in an upward planar layout. Specifically, we've developed a fixed-parameter algorithm based on the number of source vertices, an XP algorithm based on the graph's treewidth, and a fixed-parameter algorithm based on the treedepth parameter. Our novel method combines parameterized techniques with SPQR tree-decompositions, extending previous tractability findings on series-parallel graphs. Moreover, we've devised a fixed-parameter algorithm for recognizing Eulerian series-parallel graphs within the context of the stated parameters.

The rising intricacy of modern adaptable systems demands elevated automation in their configuration process, thus also accelerating development cycles via rapid, automated workflow integration. A novel automated configuration framework is introduced, using model checking and SMT, adaptable to any domain definable by SMT formulas, allowing for modular scalability and improved human understanding via metric-driven optimization. Its effectiveness is demonstrated through its application to configuring a CGRA memory tile for diverse image processing tasks.

This study examines the operator growth phenomenon in Lie-symmetric systems by utilizing concepts from quantum information theory. We specifically analyze Krylov complexity, entanglement properties, and information capacity within SU(1,1) and SU(2) symmetric systems, leveraging two-mode coherent states as a primary tool. These coherent states enable us to explore operator growth patterns and entanglement structures in a systematic manner, ultimately verifying that certain fundamental Lie-symmetric systems exhibit quadratic growth behavior similar to that observed in near-integrable systems. Moreover, we establish a near-integrability mapping for Lie-symmetric systems, revealing deep connections between their shared mathematical structures.

Recently, WiFi has become the primary method for locating individuals or devices within indoor settings. To facilitate this process, WiFi fingerprinting, a technique where reference measurements with known locations are collected and analyzed, has become a standard approach in positioning methods and algorithms discussed in academic literature. However, measuring spatial distances between these collected data sets is often based on simple metrics like Received Signal Strength (RSS) based Euclidean distance, which many researchers have agreed do not provide accurate position estimates. This is attributed to the non-line-of-sight nature of WiFi signal propagation. In an effort to address this limitation, our proposed method deviates from conventional linear modeling techniques commonly used in position estimation. Instead, we leverage a well-established non-linear physical characteristic of WiFi signal propagation, specifically the log-normal shadowing model. By utilizing the maximum likelihood estimator in conjunction with this model, we can derive both coarse and precise indoor positions from collected data sets. To demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, extensive experiments were carried out in a real-world indoor environment. Our experimental results consistently outperform existing methods, showing an average 22.1 meter (or 80.9%) reduction in positioning error.
